title: Rage all you like, His help still comes.
subtitle: Anger at the truth succeeding changes nothing

row.title: the one who thinks
sub: Allah will not help him ﷺ

then: Ibn Abbas explained it as being about whoever thinks Allah will not support Muhammad ﷺ. {trap}If it annoys him so much, let him do his worst{/trap}, then see if it cures the rage in his heart. Allah will certainly help His Messengers.
now: A colleague gets the promotion you wanted, and every success they have makes your chest tight. You replay it at night. {idea}Your fury does not move their path an inch; it only burns you.{/idea}
old: If I stay angry enough, maybe what I hate will stop.
new: Rage at what Allah has decided harms only me; letting go is the real relief.
try: Name one thing you are angry about that you cannot change. Hand it over in a short dua.

title: Clear verses, sent down, and guidance is His.
subtitle: The Quran is clear; hearts are guided by Allah

row.title: guidance is a gift
sub: ask the One who gives it

then: Ibn Kathir says the Quran is {idea}clear in its wording and its meaning{/idea}, evidence from Allah to people. Who accepts it is in Allah's hands, and He has full wisdom in that. The rage of the last verse cannot change it.
now: You have explained something to a friend five times, with links and examples, and they still do not see it. Or you read a verse ten times and it suddenly clicks one night. {reward}Clarity is on the page; the opening of the heart is His.{/reward}
old: If I explain it better, anyone will accept the truth.
new: My job is to be clear; turning a heart belongs to Allah.
try: Before reading the Quran today, ask Allah in one line to open your heart to it.

title: Every group named, and Allah alone will judge them.
subtitle: The final verdict between all beliefs is His

row.title: Allah
sub: witness to all, on the Day

then: The verse names the faith communities known to its listeners. Ibn Kathir says Allah will {idea}judge between them with justice{/idea}, for He is Witness over their deeds and knows what they say and hide.
now: Online, everyone has a verdict on who is saved and who is not, in a single comment. {idea}The verse quietly takes that job out of your hands.{/idea} Your task is your own belief and conduct, which He also witnesses.
old: I need to settle who is right and who is wrong, today.
new: Allah will judge between everyone; I answer for what I believe and do.
try: Skip one argument about other people's fate today. Spend the time on your own prayer.

title: Sun, stars, trees and animals all bow to Him.
subtitle: A verse of prostration: all creation bows
then: Ibn Kathir says everything prostrates to Allah {idea}in a way that fits its nature{/idea}. Sun, moon and stars are named because some worshipped them, yet they too bow. He records the Prophet ﷺ saying that when a person prostrates at such a verse, Shaytan withdraws weeping.
now: You are on a hill at sunset, phone up for a photo. The sun slides down, the trees sway, birds settle. {reward}Everything around you is already bowing.{/reward} The only one deciding is you.
old: Prostration is something I do when I get around to it.
new: The whole world is already bowing; I am invited to join it freely.
try: Make one extra, unhurried sujood today and stay there a few breaths longer.

title: Two sides that disputed about their Lord.
subtitle: Believers and deniers, and what denial earns

row.title: deniers
sub: want to put out its light

then: Abu Dharr swore this was revealed about the single combat at Badr: Hamzah, Ali and Ubaydah against Utbah, Shaybah and Al-Walid. Mujahid and Ata said it covers {idea}believers and disbelievers{/idea} in general, and Ibn Jarir favored that wider view.
now: You do not need a battlefield to pick a side. It happens in small moments: when the office mocks prayer and you laugh along or stay quiet with dignity. {idea}Every day you lean toward one side or the other.{/idea}
old: Believing or not is a private opinion with no real stakes.
new: Which side I stand on about my Lord is the most serious choice I make.
try: Today, in one small moment, quietly stand on the side of your faith.

title: The punishment reaches inside, not only the surface.
subtitle: A warning that goes deeper than skin
then: Continuing the description of those who disbelieved from verse 19. Ibn Kathir explains the boiling water reaches {trap}what is within them as well as their skins{/trap}. The listeners heard a warning about a Day that leaves nothing hidden.
now: You keep the outside polished: the profile, the smile at work, the neat car. Inside, something you know is wrong keeps growing. {idea}The verse reminds you the inside counts too{/idea}, and the inside can still be cleaned today.
old: As long as I look fine on the outside, I am fine.
new: What is inside me matters most, and it is not too late to repair it.
try: Seek forgiveness today for one private wrong no one else knows about.

title: Iron, where they once had power.
subtitle: The strength they relied on reversed
then: Still describing those who disbelieved. Ibn Abbas said they will be {trap}struck with these rods{/trap}. Those who once used strength to oppose the believers will face a power they cannot resist.
now: Maybe you have power over someone: a younger sibling, an employee, a tenant. It is easy to use it carelessly. {idea}This verse is a sober reminder that all power is borrowed{/idea}, and can be turned around.
old: My position means I can treat people however I want.
new: Every bit of power I hold is on loan and will be asked about.
try: Use whatever authority you have today to make one person's day easier.

title: Every time they try to leave, they are turned back.
subtitle: No escape there, so the exit is here
then: Ibn Kathir notes the words said to them are {trap}a humiliation by word and deed{/trap}, like the verse about tasting the Fire they used to deny. The listeners in Makkah were told plainly that escape would not be possible then.
now: You keep saying you will change after this exam, after this job, after the wedding. {reward}The verse is mercy in a hard shape:{/reward} the door that will be shut later is wide open right now.
old: I can always sort things out with Allah later.
new: The only sure moment to turn back is this one.
try: Stop one thing today you have been planning to quit later.

title: Silk instead of fire, gold instead of chains.
subtitle: The garments of the people of the gardens
then: Ibn Kathir notes the contrast: right after {trap}garments of fire{/trap} come {reward}garments of silk{/reward}. He cites the Prophet ﷺ saying the believer's adornment there reaches as far as their wudu reached.
now: You are washing your hands and arms for wudu before work, water on the cold tiles, nobody watching. {reward}Those simple strokes are where the jewelry of the gardens will shine.{/reward}
old: Small acts like wudu are just routine.
new: Each wudu is marking the places that will be adorned.
try: Make your next wudu slowly and fully, remembering where it reaches.

title: Guided to good words, guided to the Praiseworthy.
subtitle: How the people of the gardens got there
then: Ibn Kathir gives several meanings that fit together: in Paradise they are led to a place of {reward}greetings of peace{/reward}; in this world they were guided to the Quran, to la ilaha illallah, and to the straight path.
now: Think about the words that fill your day: the podcasts, the group chat, the gossip at lunch. {idea}The people of the gardens were guided to good words here first.{/idea} What you speak now is practice for what you will hear then.
old: The words I use every day do not matter much.
new: Good speech is a path; the gardens are where it leads.
try: Replace one complaint today with a sentence of praise to Allah.

title: A House made for all people, and those who blocked it.
subtitle: The Sacred Mosque belongs equally to everyone
then: From here the style changes; the surah introduction places these verses in the first Dhul-Hijjah in Madinah. The emigrants missed Makkah and the Hajj. Ibn Kathir says the Quraysh {trap}prevented the believers from reaching the Sacred Mosque{/trap}, though Allah made it equal for those living there and those coming from far.
now: You see a newcomer at your local mosque, unsure where to stand, and the regulars glance over as if they own the place. {idea}The verse says the House belongs to all who come{/idea}, whoever got there first.
old: The people who were here first get to decide who belongs.
new: Allah's House is open equally; I am a guest there like everyone else.
try: Next time at the mosque, greet someone new and help them find their place.

title: Ibrahim was shown the spot, and told: no partners.
subtitle: Why the House was built in the first place

row.title: Ibrahim
sub: shown the site of the House

row.title: associate nothing
sub: build it in My Name alone

then: Ibn Kathir says this is {trap}a rebuke to Quraysh{/trap}, who set up partners in the very place founded on worshipping Allah alone. Allah guided Ibrahim to the site, and Qatadah and Mujahid said purify means purify it from shirk.
now: Your heart can be like that House: built for Allah, but slowly crowded with other things you lean on, like approval, money, a screen. {idea}Ibrahim's job was to clear the space.{/idea} Yours can be the same.
old: There is room in my heart for Allah alongside everything else I cling to.
new: A House built for One stays pure when I clear out what competes with Him.
try: Tidy your prayer space today and pray there with your phone in another room.

title: Call them, and they will come from every distant road.
subtitle: Ibrahim's call to Hajj, still answered
then: Ibn Kathir reports Ibrahim asking how his voice could reach people. {idea}He was told: call them, and We will convey it.{/idea} He links the verse to Ibrahim's prayer that hearts would long for his family, and says every Muslim longs to see the Ka'bah.
now: You post one small reminder, or teach your kid one dua at bedtime, and think it is too little to matter. {reward}Ibrahim's one call is still being answered by millions every year.{/reward} Your part is to call.
old: What I do is too small to reach anyone.
new: I do the calling; Allah decides how far it travels.
try: Share one good word or reminder with one person today, and leave the rest to Allah.
